part2_method: mfcc_cosine_nn, fixed threshold >=0.995, n_neighbors=2 within-train self-search (n=3000)
verdict: Likely almost entirely false positives. Reproducing the same self-search on the same 3,000-clip sample, a per-query z-score check (top-1 similarity vs. that clip's own similarity distribution across the other 2,999 clips) finds a maximum z-score of 2.56 -- far below any defensible outlier threshold (e.g. z>=8). A fixed 0.995 cosine threshold on this 40-dim MFCC mean+std fingerprint is not selective at this pool size: unrelated clips already average ~0.97 similarity on this fingerprint, so picking the single most-similar match out of ~3,000 candidates exceeds 0.995 for the large majority of queries by chance alone, independent of real duplication.
recommendation: Do not use duplicate_pairs.parquet's pair list or 1,973-pair count for any split-design decision as-is. Re-derive with a z-score-relative criterion (or a more discriminative fingerprint) before concluding anything about within-train duplication rate.
